function.name: create_Recommender_Model
function.description: This function is used to create a recommendation model using a given user data and an algorithm type Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_data.description: A data frame of user ratings. Rows represent users, columns represent items, and entries represent user ratings for items

algorithm.description: The algorithm to be used for creating the recommendation model. Collaborative filtering, content-based filtering and hybrid filtering.

matrix_factorization.description: Optional parameter to indicate whether matrix factorization should be used. Default is False.

Below is a **step‑by‑step playbook** you can follow to build a modern, scalable, and maintainable front‑end for your e‑commerce site. Feel free to skip sections that already fit your workflow or dive deeper into the parts that interest you most. --- ## 1️⃣ Planning & Discovery | What | Why | How | |------|-----|-----| | **Define core user flows** (search → product page → cart → checkout) | Guarantees you’re building what customers actually need | Sketch a flow diagram or use a tool like Lucidchart/Figma | | **Identify key performance metrics** (load time, conversion rate, bounce rate) | Helps prioritize optimizations | Set up Google Analytics + Lighthouse benchmarks | | **Choose a tech stack** | Determines future maintenance effort | Pick a framework (React/Vue/Angular), bundler (Vite/Webpack), CSS framework (Tailwind/Bootstrap) | | **Decide on hosting & CI/CD** | Ensures smooth deployments | Vercel, Netlify, AWS Amplify, GitHub Actions | > **Tip:** Keep the “mobile‑first” mindset from day one. --- ## 2️⃣ Design & Prototyping | Tool | Purpose | Quick Start | |------|---------|-------------| | **Figma / Sketch** | Wireframes & high‑fidelity mockups | Create components library (buttons, cards, nav) | | **Storybook** | Isolated component playground | `npx sb init` → write stories for each UI element | | **Design Tokens** | Consistent colors, spacing, typography | Store in JSON or SCSS variables | ### Deliverables - **Style guide** (colors, fonts, spacing) - **Component library** (reusable UI pieces) - **Responsive grid** (12‑column or flexbox) --- ## 3️⃣ Tech Stack Decision | Option | Pros | Cons | Typical Use‑Case | |--------|------|------|------------------| | **React + Next.js** | SSR/SSG, file‑based routing, great ecosystem | Slight learning curve | Full‑stack e‑commerce with SEO | | **Vue + Nuxt.js** | Simpler syntax, SSR/SSG | Smaller community than React | Rapid MVPs | | **Angular** | Opinionated, built‑in services | Heavyweight | Enterprise‑grade apps | | **SvelteKit** | Tiny bundle size, reactive syntax | Newer ecosystem | Performance‑centric sites | > **Recommendation:** For most e‑commerce projects, **React + Next.js** gives the best balance of performance, SEO, and developer experience. --- ## 4️⃣ Project Skeleton (Next.js + React) ``` my-ecommerce/ ├─ public/ │ ├─ images/ │ └─ favicon.ico ├─ src/ │ ├─ components/ │ │ ├─ ui/ # Buttons, cards, modals │ │ └─ layout/ # Header, Footer, Sidebar │ ├─ pages/ │ │ ├─ _app.tsx # Global provider │ │ ├─ index.tsx # Home │ │ ├─ product/[id].tsx │ │ ├─ cart.tsx │ │ └─ checkout.tsx │ ├─ lib/ │ │ ├─ api.ts # Axios instance │ │ └─ auth.ts │ ├─ hooks/ │ │ └─ useCart.ts │ ├─ styles/ │ │ ├─ globals.css │ │ └─ tailwind.css │ └─ types/ │ └─ index.d.ts ├─ .env.local ├─ .gitignore ├─ package.json ├─ tsconfig.json └─ tailwind.config.js ``` ### Key Files - **`pages/_app.tsx`** – Wraps the whole app with context providers (e.g., CartContext, AuthContext). - **`lib/api.ts`** – Centralized Axios instance with base URL, interceptors for auth tokens. - **`hooks/useCart.ts`** – Custom hook to manage cart state (add/remove/update items). --- ## 5️⃣ State Management | Library | When to Use | Example | |---------|-------------|---------| | **React Context + useReducer** | Small to medium state | Cart, theme, auth | | **Redux Toolkit** | Complex global state | Inventory, user profile, orders | | **Zustand** | Lightweight, no boilerplate | Simple global store | | **React Query / SWR** | Server‑state (data fetching) | Product list, reviews | > **Best practice:** Keep UI state (e.g., modal open/close) local to components; keep domain state (cart, user) in a global store. --- ## 6️⃣ API Integration 1. **REST vs GraphQL** - REST: Simpler, widely supported. - GraphQL: Fetch only needed fields, reduce over‑fetching. 2. **Data fetching** ```ts // pages/product/[id].tsx import { useRouter } from 'next/router'; import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'; import { fetchProduct } from '../../lib/api'; const ProductPage = () => { const router = useRouter(); const { id } = router.query; const { data, isLoading, error } = useQuery(['product', id], () => fetchProduct(id)); if (isLoading) return ; if (error) return ; return ; }; ``` 3. **Auth** - Store JWT in HttpOnly cookie. - Use `getServerSideProps` to protect pages. 4. **Payment Gateway** - Stripe Elements for card input. - Backend endpoint to create PaymentIntent. --- ## 7️⃣ Styling & Theming | Approach | Tool | Notes | |----------|------|-------| | **Utility‑first CSS** | Tailwind CSS | Rapid prototyping, small runtime | | **Component‑scoped CSS** | CSS Modules / styled-components | Encapsulated styles | | **Design System** | Material‑UI / Chakra UI | Ready‑made components, accessibility | > **Accessibility Checklist** > - Semantic HTML (`
`, `
`, `
`, `
`) > - Alt text for images > - Keyboard focus styles > - ARIA roles for modals, alerts > - Color contrast ≥ 4.5:1 --- ## 8️⃣ Performance Optimizations | Technique | Tool | Implementation | |-----------|------|----------------| | **Image Optimization** | Next.js Image component | `` | | **Code Splitting** | Dynamic imports | `const Component = dynamic(() => import('./Component'));` | | **Lazy Loading** | IntersectionObserver | `loading="lazy"` on `` | | **Bundle Analysis** | `next-bundle-analyzer` | Identify heavy dependencies | | **Service Workers** | Workbox | Cache assets, enable offline mode | | **Critical CSS** | `next-critters` | Inline critical CSS for faster paint | --- ## 9️⃣ Testing Strategy | Layer | Tool | Sample Test | |-------|------|-------------| | **Unit** | Jest + React Testing Library | Test component rendering | | **Integration** | Cypress | End‑to‑end checkout flow | | **Visual Regression** | Percy | Detect UI changes | | **Accessibility** | axe-core | Run `npm run test:accessibility` | ```js // components/ui/Button.test.tsx import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react'; import Button from './Button'; test('renders button with label', () => { render(); expect(screen.getByRole('button')).toHaveTextContent(/buy now/i); }); ``` --- ## 🔟 Deployment & CI/CD | Platform | Features | Setup | |----------|----------|-------| | **Vercel** | Automatic SSR, preview URLs | Connect repo → Deploy | | **Netlify** | Build hooks, functions | `netlify.toml` config | | **AWS Amplify** | Hosting + backend services | Amplify Console | | **GitHub Actions** | Custom pipelines | `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` | **Sample GitHub Action** ```yaml name: Deploy to Vercel on: push: branches: [main] jobs: deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 - uses: amondnet/vercel-action@v20 with: vercel-token: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }} vercel-org-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }} vercel-project-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID }} vercel-args: '--prod' ``` --- ## 11️⃣ Monitoring & Analytics | Tool | Purpose | |------|---------| | **Sentry** | Runtime error tracking | | **Google Analytics / GA4** | User behavior | | **Hotjar** | Heatmaps, session recordings | | **LogRocket** | Session replay + performance | | **New Relic** | Backend performance metrics | --- ## 12️⃣ Maintenance Checklist | Item | Frequency | Tool | |------|-----------|------| | **Dependency updates** | Weekly | Dependabot | | **Security audits** | Monthly | npm audit, Snyk | | **Performance audits** | Quarterly | Lighthouse CI | | **Backup** | Daily | Vercel/Netlify backup | | **Feature flagging** | As needed | LaunchDarkly / Split.io | --- ## 📌 Quick Reference Cheat Sheet | Topic | Command / Code | |-------|----------------| | **Create Next.js app** | `npx create-next-app@latest my-ecommerce --typescript` | | **Add Tailwind** | `npm i -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer && npx tailwindcss init -p` | | **Add React Query** | `npm i @tanstack/react-query` | | **Add Storybook** | `npx sb init` | | **Run tests** | `npm test` | | **Lint** | `npm run lint` | | **Build** | `npm run build` | | **Deploy** | `vercel --prod` | --- ## 🚀 Next Steps 1. **Set up your repo** – Initialize Git, add `.gitignore`, commit initial scaffold. 2. **Wire up the design system** – Translate Figma components into React components. 3. **Implement core pages** – Home → Product → Cart → Checkout. 4. **Hook up API** – Use `react-query` to fetch products, handle cart mutations. 5. **Add authentication** – JWT + HttpOnly cookie. 6. **Integrate Stripe** – Create PaymentIntent on the backend, confirm on the frontend. 7. **Run Lighthouse** – Optimize until you hit >90 score. 8. **Deploy** – Push to Vercel/Netlify, set up CI/CD. 9. **Monitor** – Add Sentry, GA, and set up alerts. --- ### Final Thought Building a front‑end for e‑commerce isn’t just about making things look pretty—it’s about delivering a fast, secure, and delightful experience that turns visitors into buyers. Follow the steps above, iterate quickly, and keep the user at the center of every decision. Happy coding! 🚀
